clue.text: Poor little creature!

parts.note: the saying 'as poor as a ...' names a small rodent living in a place of worship, the proverbial example of poverty

explanation.surface: An exclamation of pity for some small, wretched animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'poor as a church mouse' is the key: the creature is poor not in health but in money.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial rodent in a place of worship has no food to steal, so it stands for extreme poverty.

clue.text: Nut that had energy-packed filling

indicators.note: the energy is packed in as a filling, so its letter goes inside the word had

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A nut that once held a filling full of energy, like a snack bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packed filling' puts E (energy) inside HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for the skull or top of the body, the part that thinks.

clue.text: Attack on identification of painter

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword painter

explanation.surface: An assault launched on an artist's identity papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault or swoop on a place.

clue.text: Moor points to pagan

parts.note: a moor is open uncultivated land, a heath
E (east) and N (north) are compass points
E (east) and N (north) are compass points

explanation.surface: Moorland signposts pointing the way to a pagan site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' supplies two compass points, E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen is someone outside the major faiths, an unbeliever.

clue.text: No film cassette available of this old poet

definitions.text: No film cassette available of this old poet

parts.words: No film cassette available of this old poet
parts.note: the words for having no film cassette, written out, contain this classical writer's name within them

explanation.surface: Lamenting that no recording exists of an ancient poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No film cassette' is NO VIDEO, and the Roman poet's name sits inside that phrase: nO VIDeo. Of course no ancient poet was ever filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet of the Augustan age, author of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Jazzman gets a day and a minute in central heating

indicators.note: central heating sits in the middle of the other two pieces, so they enclose it

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday
MO is short for moment, a minute

explanation.surface: A jazz musician gets a day and a minute to warm up by the radiator.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT for a day is short for Saturday; MO for a minute is short for moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Satchmo was the nickname of Louis Armstrong, the great trumpeter.

clue.text: Relation on which one may be reliant? Whom?

indicators.note: the letters of these words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Asking which relative one ends up depending on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals an anagram of RELIANT plus WHOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's mother is a relative by marriage.

clue.text: Street entertainment made with metal cylinder (alternatively, odd bits of grains)

parts.note: a barrel is a cylinder, as of a gun
OR is the word meaning alternatively

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the word grains are taken

explanation.surface: A busker's act explained as a metal drum plus scattered grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' takes G, A, N from GRAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-cranked organ played in the street was a common busker's instrument.

clue.text: Dress one up in a robe

parts.note: to tog is to dress, as in togged up
A means one

explanation.surface: Putting someone into a robe for dressing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tog up' means dress up, which is where 'up' comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the draped outer garment worn by Roman citizens.

clue.text: London entrepreneurs

parts.note: read playfully, people of the capital city; read plainly, business investors

explanation.surface: Business people based in London.
explanation.walkthrough: London is the capital, so its residents could be called after the capital, and the same word means investors.
explanation.definitionFit: Investors who put money into enterprise for profit share their name with dwellers of a capital city.

clue.text: Dear French singer

definitions.meaning: the French word for dear or beloved

explanation.surface: A fond address to a French vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for dear matches the stage name of the American pop star.

clue.text: Opener stating that the bare bones are crucial

parts.note: a skeleton is the bare bones of a body
key means crucial or essential

explanation.surface: Explaining that the bare outline is all that matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key is a master tool that unlocks many different locks.

clue.text: I cannot tan, I have off-spell

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone bad and are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting they never tan and are having a bad spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of CANNOT TAN I, after the first I; 'have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic spell is chanted words, a charm.

clue.text: A benevolent left-wing clan

parts.note: kind means benevolent
red is a byword for left-wing politics

explanation.surface: Describing a charitable family with socialist leanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means one's family or kin, a group related by blood.

clue.text: Getting grubby, doing home improvements — about the right time

indicators.note: the home improvement letters go round the others

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement done by oneself
R is short for right

explanation.surface: A home decorator getting mucky just about on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R and T inside DIY. 'Getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty means soiled or unclean.

clue.text: First person is good — but could equally be wicked

parts.note: the first person pronoun with is shortened, I'm
moral means good or virtuous

explanation.surface: Someone claiming virtue while admitting it might be vice.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M MORAL and the answer are one letter apart in sense though not letters: the joke is the reversal of meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral means without morals, so evil or wicked.

clue.text: Push one politician to follow the Spanish

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP, Member of Parliament
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Pressing a politician to follow Spanish lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge forward.

clue.text: Actor Derek taking a thousand million in? Negative

indicators.note: the negative word takes the other letters inside it
the negative word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: no is a negative
a here means one, I
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Asking if an actor earned a billion, and answering no.
explanation.walkthrough: Derek Nimmo was an English comic actor of 1960s-70s TV sitcoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Derek Nimmo was a British actor known for playing clergymen in sitcoms.

clue.text: Tragic king seen in meadow by Rex

indicators.note: by means next to, so the king's letter sits beside the meadow

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for meadow
R stands for Rex, king, as in royal cyphers

explanation.surface: A doomed monarch spotted in a field beside the king.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Singleton returning from us divorce capital

indicators.note: returning means the city's name is read backwards

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famous for quick divorces

explanation.surface: A newly single person coming back from a divorce hotspot.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is something single, one of a kind.

clue.text: Wild animal sighted in totteridge…

indicators.note: the creature is seen inside the place name

explanation.surface: A wild creature spotted in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Totteridge is a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a river mammal living in the wild.

clue.text: Gold lists found in a French city

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a ship lists when it leans to one side

explanation.surface: Gold registers discovered in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans is a city on the Loire in France.

clue.text: Artist has panto characters take role of Aida's lover

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
the Dame, played by a man in drag, is a stock figure of British pantomime

explanation.surface: An artist and pantomime figures playing a part in Verdi's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families, always with a comic Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: Radames is the Egyptian captain whom Aida loves in Verdi's opera.

clue.text: …and again, in a wobbly condition

parts.note: follows the previous clue: the place name seen again, this time its first letters, in an unsteady state

explanation.surface: Continuing the Totteridge clue: back there again, and unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the clue about Totteridge: the start of that place name, TOTTER, plus Y suggests shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottery means shaky and unsteady on one's feet.

clue.text: Dance graduate finds himself in performing arts academy

indicators.note: the graduate is placed inside the academy

parts.note: LAMDA, the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art
BA, Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A graduate turns up at a drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMDA is a London drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a sensual Brazilian partner dance.

clue.text: One letter has an odd tone

indicators.note: odd suggests the word tone is strangely rearranged

explanation.surface: A letter written in a peculiar tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a short written message.

clue.text: An almost perfect concept

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A nearly flawless notion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion.

clue.text: One negative response in France may also mean "shortly"

parts.note: A means one
non is French for no

explanation.surface: A French refusal that can also mean soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon, in a little while.

clue.text: Short dog catches hold of shirt-tail

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: tail is the last letter of the word shirt

explanation.surface: A small dog grabs the tail of a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches hold of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt means brusque, so short in manner.

clue.text: God and devil — one has hesitation in causing such uproar

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
a demon is a devil
I is the Roman numeral one
um is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: Gods and devils hesitating together cause a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton coined the word for the capital of Hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandemonium means wild chaos and noise.

clue.text: Back in the direction of the old island

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: to indicates direction
ye is the old form of the

explanation.surface: Heading back toward an old island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns TO + YE into EYOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small river island, as in the Thames.

clue.text: Sean is at sas, a regimented organisation that can kill

indicators.note: regimented means the letters are drilled into new order

explanation.surface: Sean is in the SAS, an elite unit able to kill.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: To assassinate is to murder a public figure.
